issues.label: Jurisdiction to decide petition
issues.why: The court must confirm it had authority under R.C. 2953.21 to rule on the petition in both case numbers.

issues.label: Petition timeliness
issues.why: The court must determine whether each petition was filed within the statutory deadline or qualifies for an exception.

issues.label: Trigger date for deadline
issues.why: The court must identify the correct start date for the filing period (e.g., direct appeal conclusion/expiration) for each case.

issues.label: Effect of pending direct appeal
issues.why: The court must address whether a petition filed while a direct appeal was pending is procedurally proper and how it should be handled.

issues.label: Successive/duplicative petitions
issues.why: The court must determine whether the filing is a first petition or is barred/limited as a successive petition by prior litigation.

issues.label: Proper statutory subsection
issues.why: The court must decide whether mis-citing R.C. 2953.21(C) (death penalty) affects viability or whether the claim is cognizable under the correct provisions.

issues.label: Cognizable claims in PCR
issues.why: The court must confirm the ineffective-assistance claim and any related constitutional claims are within the scope of postconviction relief.

issues.label: Res judicata bar
issues.why: The court must decide whether issues raised or that could have been raised on direct appeal are barred in postconviction.

issues.label: Mootness determination correctness
issues.why: The court must assess whether Johnson I actually moots the ineffective-assistance claim or merely disposes of record-based issues.

issues.label: Law-of-the-case impact
issues.why: The court must determine which findings from Johnson I bind the trial court on postconviction issues.

issues.label: Different case numbers analysis
issues.why: The court must separately analyze eligibility, timeliness, and merits for 22CRC-I0144 and 22CRC-I0207 rather than treating them as one case.

issues.label: No contest case finality
issues.why: The court must confirm the final, appealable order status and appellate history in 22CRC-I0207 to apply postconviction rules correctly.

issues.label: New evidence definition
issues.why: The court must decide whether the proffered material qualifies as evidence outside the trial record for postconviction purposes.

issues.label: Affidavit credibility assessment
issues.why: If affidavits support the petition, the court must apply the Calhoun factors (or equivalent) to assess credibility without a hearing.

issues.label: Operative facts pleaded
issues.why: The court must determine whether the petition alleges sufficient operative facts to establish substantive grounds for relief.

issues.label: Supporting materials sufficiency
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether documentary support meets statutory requirements and is properly authenticated/competent evidence.

issues.label: Discovery availability limits
issues.why: The court must consider whether the petitioner sought discovery and the limited entitlement to discovery in PCR proceedings.

issues.label: IAC Strickland performance prong
issues.why: The court must analyze whether counsel’s actions/omissions fell below an objective standard of reasonableness.

issues.label: IAC Strickland prejudice prong
issues.why: The court must determine whether there is a reasonable probability of a different outcome absent counsel’s alleged errors.

issues.label: Plea context prejudice standard
issues.why: Because convictions followed pleas, the court must apply the Hill v. Lockhart standard (would defendant have insisted on trial).

issues.label: Plea voluntariness overlap
issues.why: The court must distinguish an IAC claim from a direct challenge to plea voluntariness already litigated and decide what remains.

issues.label: Record-based vs extra-record
issues.why: The court must separate claims resolvable from the existing record (appeal) from those requiring extra-record evidence (PCR).

issues.label: Evidentiary hearing entitlement
issues.why: The court must decide whether the petition and files/records show substantive grounds for relief requiring a hearing under R.C. 2953.21.

issues.label: Standard for denying hearing
issues.why: The court must apply the correct legal standard (not discretion alone) for when a hearing may be denied.

issues.label: Proper standard of review
issues.why: On appeal, the court must identify the correct review standards (legal error vs abuse of discretion) for hearing denial and findings adequacy.

issues.label: Findings of fact requirement
issues.why: R.C. 2953.21(H) requires findings of fact and conclusions of law when dismissing; the court must ensure compliance.

issues.label: Conclusions of law requirement
issues.why: The court must provide legal reasoning tied to each claim to permit meaningful appellate review.

issues.label: Adequacy under Penland
issues.why: The court must meet Penland’s mandate that findings/conclusions be sufficient and address the petitioner’s claims, not merely be conclusory.

issues.label: Address each claim separately
issues.why: The court must ensure its entry resolves each distinct ground for relief raised as to each case.

issues.label: Incorporation by reference limits
issues.why: If the court relies on prior decisions (e.g., Johnson I), it must explain how they dispose of the postconviction claims and any extra-record evidence.

issues.label: Forfeiture specification issues
issues.why: For 22CRC-I0207, the court must consider whether counsel-related claims affect the forfeiture order and whether forfeiture is within PCR scope.

issues.label: Remedy scope if relief granted
issues.why: The court must identify appropriate relief (vacate plea/conviction, new hearing, resentencing) tailored to the proven constitutional violation.

issues.label: Harmless error consideration
issues.why: If procedural error occurred (e.g., inadequate findings), the court must decide whether it is reversible or harmless given the record.

issues.label: Procedural default/waiver
issues.why: The court must determine whether any claims were waived by plea, by failure to raise earlier, or by not attaching required materials.

issues.label: Consolidation/procedural handling
issues.why: The court must consider whether the petitions were properly docketed/ruled upon in both cases and whether separate entries are required.

issues.label: Notice and service compliance
issues.why: The court must ensure statutory notice/service requirements for postconviction proceedings were satisfied before dismissal.

issues.label: Need for prosecutorial response
issues.why: The court must consider whether the State filed a response and whether the court relied on materials outside the record without giving notice/opportunity to respond.
